## bijection_verdict
**PASS.** Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts): the increase-limit and retention baselines restate the arithmetic of the base clauses their overwrites retire, so the corpus carries the same formula once as "no longer in force" and once as the computation document's method — faithful to the source. First revision.

## dependency_form
- Prerequisite sentences: both stand verbatim, state form, on the blocked side only; their "Stated in terms of the record" / "In the words of the record" restatements stay in the state form and name no tool, write or problem. Not RED.
- Blind-audit hop marks: both hops state-derived; none pre-solved.
- No other problem's tool name in the blocked documents; no route, checklist, step list or chain-walking example; titles general.
- `good_standing_payment_terms` "A payment that replaces a payment the bank returned is not a good-standing payment …" is the source rule's own scope sentence, not a dependency.
- **KB-EXPLICIT RED — computation document hints that something modifies it.**
  - symptom: the baseline computation document for the increase limit says the limit percentage can fall and is held at zero, although in that document the limit percentage is a fixed class figure.
  - evidence: `increase_limit_rent_computation_6ba91429.json`, `## Definitions`, bullet "Limit percentage": "**Limit percentage** — the class's largest single increase. The limit percentage is never less than zero (0 percent), so the limit rent never falls below the rent before the increase." The class figures it names are 7–15 percent (`rent_change_terms_by_class`), so the floor has no effect unless something subtracts from the percentage.
  - root cause: the zero floor comes from the overwrite's replaced_by order ("first the limit percentage is the tenure maximum less the recent-increase, prepaid-plan, lien-record and lateness reductions, never less than zero, so that a reduction never sets the rent below the rent before the increase …"). It concerns how the reductions combine, but it was put in the baseline document. No factor document carries it (grep: "less than zero" / "below the rent before" occur only in this document). A reader of the computation document alone can tell the percentage is reduced somewhere. That is the kind of hint ("adjustments may apply") the discrete-topology rule forbids.
  - effect on this task: none on the solution (limit percentage 6% > 0; all three scored values match the GT). Recorded because a faithful corpus must still not signal its factors from the baseline.
  - affected document/location: `docs/unit/increase_limit_rent_computation_6ba91429.json`, Definitions, "Limit percentage" bullet.
- **Verdict: KB-EXPLICIT RED** (one finding).
